conditions.description: Pays employees or directors through PAYE.

profileFields.label: Company name
profileFields.description: The name on the Companies House register.

profileFields.label: Company number
profileFields.description: The number on the certificate of incorporation.

profileFields.label: Registered office address
profileFields.description: The official address on the register.

profileFields.label: SIC code
profileFields.description: The code that says what the company does.

profileFields.label: Corporation Tax UTR
profileFields.description: The Unique Taxpayer Reference HMRC sends for Corporation Tax.

profileFields.label: VAT registration number
profileFields.description: From HMRC once registered for VAT.

profileFields.label: Employer PAYE reference
profileFields.description: From HMRC once registered as an employer.

roles.label: Director
roles.description: Runs the company; at least one is needed.

roles.label: Shareholder
roles.description: Owns shares; at least one is needed and can be a director.

roles.label: Person with significant control
roles.description: Someone with significant control over the company, recorded on the register.

setupSteps.title: Choose a company name
setupSteps.description: Check the name follows the naming rules and is not taken.

setupSteps.title: Choose directors, shareholders and people with significant control
setupSteps.description: You need at least one director and one shareholder, who can be the same person. A company secretary is optional.

setupSteps.title: Verify the directors' identity
setupSteps.description: Directors and people with significant control verify their identity with Companies House and get a personal code. The company's confirmation statement is not accepted until every director has verified.

setupSteps.title: Pick a registered office and a SIC code
setupSteps.description: The registered office is the official address. The SIC code says what the company does.

setupSteps.title: Agree the memorandum and articles of association
setupSteps.description: Most companies use the model articles offered while registering.

setupSteps.title: Register the company with Companies House
setupSteps.description: Online registration is usually done within 24 hours.

typicalCost.note: Online; by post it costs more and takes 8 to 10 days.

setupSteps.title: Set up Corporation Tax
setupSteps.description: Choose it while registering, or add Corporation Tax to the business tax account afterwards.

setupSteps.title: Open a business bank account
setupSteps.description: Keep the company's money apart from your own.

setupSteps.title: Register for VAT when you have to
setupSteps.description: Register when taxable turnover for the last 12 months goes over the VAT threshold, or is expected to in the next 30 days; you can also register voluntarily. Check the current threshold on GOV.UK.

setupSteps.title: Register as an employer before the first payday
setupSteps.description: Needed to pay salaries, including to directors. You cannot register more than 2 months before you start paying people.

obligations.title: Confirmation statement
obligations.description: File at least once every 12 months. The review period ends 12 months after incorporation or the last statement; you have 14 days after it to file.

obligations.title: Annual accounts
obligations.description: Due 9 months after the financial year ends. The first accounts are due 21 months after the company was registered.

obligations.title: Pay Corporation Tax
obligations.description: Due 9 months and 1 day after the accounting period ends, for taxable profits up to £1.5 million (other rules above that). The date shown assumes the period ends on the last day of a month.

obligations.title: Company Tax Return
obligations.description: Due 12 months after the end of the accounting period it covers.

obligations.title: VAT Return
obligations.description: Usually every 3 months; file and pay one calendar month and 7 days after the period ends. The dates shown assume calendar quarters; yours may differ.

obligations.title: Full Payment Submission (FPS)
obligations.description: Report pay to HMRC on or before each payday.

obligations.title: Pay PAYE to HMRC
obligations.description: Pay by the 22nd of the next tax month (tax months run from the 6th to the 5th), or the 19th by post. Quarterly payers have other dates.

obligations.title: Report changes to Companies House
obligations.description: Within 14 days of a change to directors, the registered office, people with significant control and other registered details.

due.event: A change to the company's registered details
